correctness.rationale: For the *zero-inclusive* EFX definition, a positive-indegree comparer has value at least 1 while any other bundle contains at most one positively valued edge; only source agents can violate. A source violates exactly when some neighbor receives at least two edges, because removing a zero-valued edge leaves the source-valued shared edge. On K_{a,b}, each prescribed source forces one valid orientation; sources on opposite sides cannot coexist. Source-free orientations avoid a zero row and an all-one column in an a-by-b orientation matrix, two disjoint events. This derives F=(2^b-1)^a+(2^a-1)^b-2^{ab}+a+b for all positive a,b. Dividing by 2^{ab} and bounding the 2^{-b} corrections yields the e^{-lambda} imbalance law as a→∞, a≤b. Independently enumerated K_{1,4}, K_{2,3}, K_{3,3}: 5,17,180 valid orientations exactly. Definitions and a=1 boundary explicitly checked.

value.rationale: The exact *prevalence* of a fairness property under independent random edge allocation is natural and quantitatively distinct from whether one fair orientation exists. The sharp scale b~2^a identifies when rejection sampling or random allocations are typically fair; this is a substantive probability threshold for a canonical dense bipartite family.
